items.stem: Define the term 'cash-flow forecast'.
items.answer: An estimate of the cash inflows and cash outflows of a business, usually month by month, for a future period.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – An estimate of the cash inflows and cash outflows of a business, usually month by month, for a future period. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two benefits to a business of preparing a cash-flow forecast.
items.answer: It shows when cash shortages may occur, so an overdraft can be arranged in advance; and it is needed to support applications for loans.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark benefit, 1 mark explanation): identify shortages, plan finance, support loan applications, set targets/monitor. [4]

items.stem: Explain why the closing balance of one month is the opening balance of the next month.
items.answer: The cash the business has at the end of one month is the cash it starts with at the beginning of the next.
items.markingKey: 1 mark same cash carried forward; 1 mark link between months. [2]

items.stem: Define the term 'cash shortage'.
items.answer: A period in which a business does not have enough cash to make its planned payments.

items.stem: Explain two limitations of cash-flow forecasts.
items.answer: Sales are hard to predict, especially for new businesses; and costs may change unexpectedly, for example because of inflation or a change in the exchange rate.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark limitation, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Explain why a business with a forecast cash surplus should still monitor its cash flow.
items.answer: Actual results may differ from the forecast, so monitoring allows quick action if customers pay late or costs rise.
items.markingKey: 1 mark actual differs from forecast; 1 mark early action. [2]

items.stem: Explain two ways a business could improve its cash flow.
items.answer: Increase inflows by offering discounts for early payment or using debt factoring; and reduce or delay outflows, for example by leasing rather than buying equipment or negotiating longer credit from suppliers.
